value: How do domain prior knowledge, worked-example type and task difficulty interact to affect cognitive load and performance in algebraic problem solving, and how do the three types of cognitive load relate to motivation measures?

A 2x2x2 randomised experiment on simultaneous-equation algebra showing a three-way interaction of prior knowledge, worked-example type and task difficulty on posttest performance consistent with the expertise reversal effect, and a positive correlation between germane cognitive load and motivational interest.

quote: One hundred and sixty participants were recruited who were randomly assigned into one of eight learning conditions.

It was found that higher-prior knowledge learners performed better with completion-worked examples than full-worked examples whereas lower-prior knowledge learners performed better with full-worked examples than completion-worked examples.

quote: Cognitive load can play a key role in learners’ abilities to solve complex problems like mathematics.
Intrinsic cognitive load is defined by the difficulty of the instructional materials that cannot be changed or altered.

Extraneous cognitive load refers to the mental load caused by improper instructional design like imposing redundant information in learning materials that requires learners’ additional processing effort.

value: When extraneous load is suppressed, working memory resources are freed and become available to the germane and intrinsic load involved in solving the problem
quote: In other words, with the influence of extraneous cognitive load abated, the cognitive resources in the working memory become available for the efforts to solve complex mathematics problems that were related to germane (efforts) and intrinsic (content complexity) cognitive load.

value: High extraneous load consumes the limited working memory resources, leaving too few for germane load, which is why extraneous load lowers both germane load and the felt probability of success
quote: This is further supported by the findings of negative correlation between extraneous cognitive load and probability of success in the current study, suggesting with high extraneous cognitive load the learners would have few cognitive resources left in working memory, hence making little room for germane cognitive load in learning.
Intrinsic cognitive load is defined by the difficulty of the instructional materials that cannot be changed or altered.

Extraneous cognitive load refers to the mental load caused by improper instructional design like imposing redundant information in learning materials that requires learners’ additional processing effort.
The last type of cognitive load is germane cognitive load. It is the mental load induced by the efforts to construct new knowledge or build new schema (Sweller et al., 1998).
That is, the outcome of an instructional strategy is subject to the level of domain prior knowledge of the learner.
Task difficulty refers to the task requirements defined by the level of content difficulty and associative cognitive demands.
Completion-worked example provides partial solution steps and expect the learners to finish the rest of the problem based on partial solution.
In contrast to median split method, Liu and Reed (1994) proposed a tri-split method that divided the participants into upper-third quarter, lower-third quarter and middle-third quarter.
The task difficulty is defined based on Sweller’s (1988) production/solution step method.
